question: Why do Poly obs span ~22-29 days despite days_back=180, and can we reach 90-day validation?
verdict: 90-day validation is NOT achievable with the current CLOB prices-history API. The ~22-29 day obs span is API-limited (price history retention), not a days_back or pagination bug.
root_cause: CLOB /prices-history returns empty arrays for resolved MLB tokens whose games commenced before ~2026-04-28. When history exists, it typically covers only ~5-6 calendar days before game time (median ~6.3d), insufficient for 2h-lead backtests on older games.

gamma_resolved_events_mlb.note: start_date_min/end_date_max do not block old events in deep pages; they change sort/filter on early pages. Removing the filter adds events but does not fix price history.

sample_60d_old_event.title: St. Louis Cardinals vs. Houston Astros

recommendations: Do not expect 90-day validation until Polymarket exposes longer-retention price history or an alternative historical midpoint source is ingested.
Keep daily --force obs collection to grow a forward-looking dataset; span will increase ~1 day per day of collection, not retroactively.
Optional minor gain: paginate resolved events without start_date_min (405 vs 314 MLB events with price) — still ~24d span, not 90d.
Update VALIDATION.md gate 1 to note CLOB retention (~1 week pre-game, ~3-4 weeks of game dates) as the binding constraint.
MLB live scanner remains HOLD until obs span reaches 90d via time, not config changes.
code_fix_rationale: No safe minimal fix: increasing max_pages or days_back does not restore deleted CLOB history; date filter removal yields marginal event gain only.
